newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 27.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Monday:

* The new chairman of the House Science Committee says there is danger that the effort to build an international space station may unravel and that Russia should no longer be full partners in the project if it continues to withhold its payments at the end of February.

* Xerox Corp is one of the companies working on micro-electro-mechanical systems, or MEMS, tiny mechanical systems that sense heat, light and sound and which some say will shape the future of technology much like microchips and lasers have done already. * Republican fund-raising drives in the last election implied that those who gave at least $250,000 to the Republican Party would have special access to Congressional party members, according to solicitation letters, invitations and interviews.

* U.S. states have plenty of cash after five years of economic growth, but rather than quickly spending the money as in past periods of economic boom, they are holding on to their funds in preparation for the next business decline.
* Chechens prepare for presidential and parliamentary elections on Monday, hoping to gain global support for their sovereignty.
* Native American Indians in the Northern U.S. are enduring a brutal winter because of one of the worst blizzards in recent history and cuts in federal aid, which many depend on.
